*Key Details of the 1879 Riot Incident:*
*The Cause*: On February 8, 1879, Victorian umpire George Coulthard gave NSW batsman Billy Murdoch out (run out), causing 2,000 spectators to storm the field.
*The Conflict*: The crowd targeted Coulthard. England captain Lord Harris and player Albert Hornby were assaulted while defending him.
*X's* *Role*: As the other umpire, X was key in trying to restore order and negotiating with NSW captain Dave Gregory to continue play rather than forfeiting the match.
*Aftermath*: The riot, often cited as the first of its kind in international cricket, resulted in a temporary breakdown in cricket relations and an apology from the New South Wales Cricket Association.
X emerged with his reputation intact, leveraging the publicity from his composed handling of the situation in his subsequent successful campaign for the New South Wales Legislative Assembly.
